category_title: Students requiring structured accountability during phonics dictation
minimal_context: The student is spelling and reading a list of words with the 'ook' pattern during a phonics dictation routine.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please write down the word 'cook' on your paper.

STUDENT: c - o - o - k

TUTOR: Okay. Now write down 'look', 'hook', and 'took'.

STUDENT: It's the ook family.

TUTOR: Yes. Now I want you to sit quietly and read that list of words by yourself over and over until time is up.

STUDENT: (Slides out of his chair and begins rolling on the floor instead of reading the list individually)

options.A: Terminate the reading demands immediately and remove the spelling list and materials from the student's workspace for ten seconds.
options.B: Provide the student with the option of changing to a different spelling task at any time during the dictation routine.
options.C: Require a physical signal from the class (thumbs up or down) to verify accuracy and allow students to self-reward with a star for trying.
options.D: Use planned ignoring (e.g., walking away from the student's workspace while he is rolling on the floor during the routine).
